item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-18
item.description: Two documents from the fortnight, read against each other, say the same thing from opposite ends of the supply chain. openEuler closed its summit on 2026-11-14 reporting that cumulative domestic installations of openEuler-family operating systems will pass 22 million and that Frost & Sullivan expects it to take 61 per cent of China's new server-OS market in 2026, on 2,200-plus member organisations and 30,000-plus contributors, renaming its own category from server OS to Agentic Infra OS and setting two internal targets stated in the same breath: 80 per cent of CVEs handled with AI assistance by year-end, and 100 per cent of the community's service agents onboarded. The same fortnight, China Industrial News on 2026-11-16 ran the industry's own attempt to name the economics of giving away models — Huang Tie-jun's BAAI deputy head Ye Qiwei saying that open versus closed is an economic choice and that open source has mostly been the follower's posture, because occupying an ecological niche is what a laggard needs; Chen Bohui of the Asia Digital Economy Academy adding that a downloaded model is only step one, since running, evaluating and maintaining it all cost money, and if those capabilities remain concentrated in a few cloud platforms then profit keeps flowing to the compute provider even after the model is open. Meanwhile Zhejiang's seven-department open-source implementation opinion, in force since 2026-07-20, writes the fix into the rulebook in one clause: open-source contributions enter professional-title assessment for university teachers, talent assessment and enterprise staff appraisal — while the funding instruments it relies on are token vouchers, compute vouchers and data vouchers, and its 2027 targets are counted in projects, enterprises and demonstration sites. Installations are the metric that grows fastest and proves least; contributions are the metric that no instrument pays for. Both documents are about the same gap.
